text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
German composer JACQUES OFFENBACH was born in 1819.
Barrister and prominent defender of the Australian Chinese community, WILLIAM AH KET, was born in 1876.
Australian polar explorer GEORGE AINSWORTH, who's remembered for his description of WINSTON CHURCHILL as a "bumptious bullfrog", was born in 1878.
Australian actor ERROL FLYNN, who became a Hollywood leg*nd, was born in Tasmania in 1909.
VFL Footballer and triple Brownlow Medalist DICK REYNOLDS was born in 1915.

American keyboard player and singer BRIAN WILSON, who formed the Beachboys in 1961 (they were first called 'Kenny and the Cadets', then 'Carl and the Passions' and then 'Pendeltones') was born in 1942. Biggest hits included "I Get Around" (1964), "Help Me Rhonda" (1965), Barbara Ann" (1966) and "Good
Vibrations" (1966).
Canadian singer ANNE MURRAY, who won popularity with the songs "Snowbird" (1970) and "You Needed Me" (1978), was born in 1945.

American singer LIONEL RICHIE, who rose to fame with the Commodores and their hit "Three Times A Lady" (1978) before turning to a successful solo career with hits such as "Say You, Say Me" (1985) and "Dancing On The Ceiling" (1986), was born in 1949.
American singer/songwriter CYNDI LAUPER, whose hits included "Girls Just Want To Have Fun" (1983) and "Time After Time" (1984), was born in 1953.
American bass player with the band Van Halen, MICHAEL ANTHONY, was born in 1955.
UK bass player with Duran Duran and Power Station NIGEL JOHN TAYLOR was born in 1960.
** EVENTS **
1756 : Over 140 people who were defending Calcutta were
imprisoned by the Nawab of Bengal in the East India Company's jail; 23 survived this imprisonment in what later became known as the Black Hole of Calcutta.
1782 : The Great Seal of the United States government,
designed by WILLIAM BARTON, was adopted on this day.
1819 : The 320-ton paddle-wheel steamship Savannah became
the first steamship to cross the Atlantic. It arrived in Liverpool after a journey from Savannah, Georgia, of 27 days 11 hours.
1837 : WILLIAM IV of Great Britain died at Windsor and was
succeeded by his niece VICTORIA; she reigned until her death in 1901.
1837 : With the accession of Queen VICTORIA to the British
throne, Hanover was automatically separated from Great Britain as its law forbade women to accede to the throne.
1887 : The longest railway bridge in Britain and the
second over the River Tay in Scotland was opened. The first had collapsed in 1879, inspiring that great poem by William McGonagall, "The Tay Bridge Disaster."
1900 : The German ambassador in Peking, Baron von
KETTELER, was assassinated by Chinese troops setting off the Boxer Rebellion which sought to remove foreign influence in China.
1923 : PANCHO VILLA, Mexican revolutionary leader, was
assassinated on his farm.
1930 : LOUIS ARMSTRONG and FATS WALLER took Broadway by
storm with the opening of their hit revue "Hot Chocolates".
1944 : The battle of the Philippine Sea ended with Japan
losing almost all its remaining trained pilots and at least 4,000 seamen.
1949 : American tennis player "Gorgeous Gussie" MORAN
caused a sensation at Wimbledon by exposing lace-edged panties under her short skirt.
1956 : Radioactive rain fell across Central Australia,
generated by an atomic cloud resulting from an atomic explosion at Monte Bello. A Queensland miner measured high radioactivity in rainwater near Cloncurry.
1960 : American FLOYD PATTERSON became the first boxer to
regain the world heavyweight crown, when he knocked out Sweden's INGMAR JOHANSSON.
1963 : Russia and the United States agreed to establish
a hot-line telephone link; it was opened on August 30.
1966 : JAMES WHITE was jailed for 18 years, for his part
in the Great Train Robbery.
1968 : American athlete JIM HINES set a new world record
for the 100-metres, of 9.8 seconds.
1975 : More than 400,000 Australians were using the
Bankcard credit system.
1980 : Plans were finalised for the design of the new
Australian Parliament House in Canberra.
1983 : American tennis player JOHN McENROE began arguing
with an umpire on the first day of the Wimbledon championships.
1990 : African National Congress leader NELSON MANDELA
received a ticker-tape welcome to New York.
1990 : Plans were announced to phase-out the Routemaster,
the world famous London double-decker bus.
1994 : Five people died in a murder-suicide in the
southern New Zealand city of Dunedin.
1995 : After mounting pressure from the environmental
group Greenpeace and government ministers in Germany, Sweden, Denmark and elsewhere, Shell oil company decided not to dump the disused oil rig Brent Spar in the North Atlantic.
